docs.title: eeg-toolkit
docs.text: eegkit is a small, tested toolkit for managing, accessing and analyzing human EEG data, built the way a neuroscience lab needs it: reproducible batch analysis, a BIDS dataset, a queryable metadata catalog behind a REST API, privacy-aware metadata handling, and a simulated real-time acquisition path - all demonstrated on the PhysioNet EEGBCI motor-imagery dataset (subjects 1-10).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Area Components Analysis filtering, bad channels, epoching + rejection, band power, ERD/ERS, CSP+LDA decoding Data management BIDS conversion (mne-bids), cached batch pipeline, group summary, CLI Data access SQLite catalog, local/S3 storage abstraction, FastAPI service Privacy keyed date shifting, identifier stripping, verifiable scan Real time device ABC, MockAmplifier, ring buffer, online mu/beta power, failure handling GUI Streamlit explorer and live monitor

docs.title: Results on subjects 1-10
docs.text:
• ERD/ERS - imagining a hand movement suppresses mu (8-13 Hz) and beta power over the contralateral sensorimotor cortex (event-related desynchronization, blue). The red burst at 6-10 Hz right after the cue is the evoked response, not a real synchronization.
  • Decoding - left vs. right is classified from ~45 trials per subject with CSP+LDA; mean accuracy is about 62 %, with a wide spread: a few subjects exceed 80 %, others sit at chance. That is typical of motor-imagery BCI ("BCI illiteracy") and of this very small data set.

Start with Getting started.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    EDF[PhysioNet EEGBCI EDF] -->|to-bids + deidentify| BIDS[(BIDS dataset)]
    BIDS --> P[pipeline: preprocess → epochs → analysis]
    P --> C[(cache: epochs, PSD, ERD)]
    P --> O[outputs: CSV + figures]
    BIDS --> CAT[(Catalog - SQLite)]
    O --> CAT
    C --> ST[[Storage: Local / S3]]
    CAT --> API[FastAPI]
    ST --> API
    CAT --> GUI1[Streamlit Explorer]
    DEV[AcquisitionDevice ABC] --- MOCK[MockAmplifier]
    MOCK --> ONL[OnlineProcessor]
    ONL --> GUI2[Streamlit Live monitor]

docs.title: Layers and dependencies
docs.text:
Layer Modules Depends on Core analysis io, preprocess, epochs, analysis, viz MNE, scikit-learn Configuration / logging config, logging pydantic Data management bids, pipeline, results, cli core Data access catalog, storage, api, deidentify SQLAlchemy, FastAPI Real time realtime.* numpy/scipy (+ core analysis.spectral) GUI gui.* everything above

Dependencies point one way: the core knows nothing about the catalog, API or GUI.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
• BIDS is the system of record. The catalog indexes BIDS; it can always be rebuilt.
  • De-identify at the ingest boundary, so downstream components only see safe data.
  • Content-hash caching per stage instead of timestamps: results are reproducible and stale outputs cannot survive a config change.
  • Storage addressed by key so local disk and S3 are interchangeable.
  • Abstract device interface so a real amplifier driver replaces MockAmplifier without touching consumers; a second ScriptedDevice in the tests proves it.
  • Gap-aware online processing - correctness over continuity.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/stone-coding/eeg-toolkit && cd eeg-toolkit
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[all]"          # or choose extras: api, gui, s3, dev, docs

Python 3.10+ is required. Core dependencies: MNE-Python, mne-bids, scikit-learn, pydantic, Typer.

docs.title: Run the whole workflow
docs.text:
export EEGKIT_DEID_SALT="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"   # secret used for date shifting
eegkit download                  # PhysioNet EEGBCI, subjects 1-10 (~100 MB)
eegkit to-bids                   # BIDS dataset in data/bids (de-identified)
eegkit run -c configs/default.yaml   # preprocessing -> epochs -> analysis, per subject + group
eegkit index                     # build the metadata catalog
eegkit serve                     # REST API on :8000 (OpenAPI docs at /docs)
eegkit app                       # Streamlit GUI on :8501

Results appear under outputs/:

outputs/
  subjects/sub-001/{status.json, qc.json, bandpower.csv, erders_summary.csv,
                    decoding.json, figures/, report.md}
  group/{decoding.csv, erders_summary.csv, summary.json, figures/}
  cache/            intermediate results (epochs, PSD, ERD maps)
  catalog.sqlite

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from eegkit.io import load_subject
from eegkit.preprocess import preprocess
from eegkit.epochs import make_epochs, reject_epochs

raw = load_subject(1, [4, 8, 12], "data/raw")
clean, bads = preprocess(raw)
epochs, report = reject_epochs(make_epochs(clean))
print(report)

See the tutorial for the complete analysis.

docs.title: Privacy and de-identification
docs.text:
This is a demonstration, not a HIPAA certification

eegkit.deidentify shows a sound approach to protecting recording metadata. It has not been validated by a privacy officer, an IRB or an expert-determination process, and it must not be treated as making data HIPAA-, GDPR- or institution-compliant. The demo dataset (PhysioNet EEGBCI) is already public and pseudonymous.

docs.title: What counts as identifying in EEG data?
docs.text:
EEG files carry more than signal. Typical sources of identifying information:

Where Examples How eegkit handles it Subject block in the file header first / middle / last name, birthday, hospital ID (MRN) removed; hospital ID replaced by a keyed pseudonym; birthday dropped (not shifted) Measurement date/time meas_date, annotation reference time, BIDS scans.tsv acq_time shifted back by a per-subject offset (1-3 years) Free text experimenter, session description, project name cleared Device info amplifier serial number, site cleared Free-form metadata dicts participants rows, catalog records identifying keys dropped, date-like values shifted The signal itself rare: a name spoken or typed into an annotation not handled - review annotations

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
Keyed, deterministic shifts. The date offset and the pseudonym are derived with HMAC-SHA256(salt, label):

  • deterministic: all runs of one subject get the same shift, so within-subject intervals (days between sessions, run order, time of day) are preserved for analysis;
  • keyed: without the secret salt the offset cannot be recomputed from the label, and a different salt gives different shifts;
  • per subject: offsets differ between subjects, so recordings cannot be re-aligned by shifting everything the same amount.

The salt is read from $EEGKIT_DEID_SALT. If it is unset the code falls back to a demo salt and logs a warning - never rely on the demo salt.

Birthday dropped, age capped. A shifted birthday is still a date that can be attacked, so the birthday is removed. age_years() returns whole years at recording, capped at 89, for the cases where age is a needed covariate.

Sex and handedness are kept because they are legitimate research variables; with small cohorts they can still contribute to re-identification (see limitations).

Verifiable. scan_for_identifiers(raw, terms) walks every field of the recording's info (including nested dictionaries), the annotation reference time and annotation text, and reports where any term still occurs. The test-suite plants names, an MRN, a birthday, device serials and dates in a recording and proves that none remain

  • in the de-identified in-memory object,
  • in the raw bytes of a saved FIF file,
  • in every file of a BIDS dataset written from it.

docs.title: Where de-identification happens in the pipeline
docs.text:
raw EDF  --(eegkit to-bids, privacy.deidentify: true)-->  BIDS dataset  -->  catalog / API

De-identification runs at the ingest boundary: everything downstream (batch pipeline, SQLite catalog, REST API, GUI) only ever sees de-identified data. The catalog schema has no columns for names or birth dates by design. A stand-alone command is also available:

EEGKIT_DEID_SALT=... eegkit deidentify raw.fif clean.fif --label sub-001

docs.title: Limitations and what a real deployment needs
docs.text:
• Subject labels must be study codes, never medical record numbers or initials.
  • Linkage risk: rare combinations of sex, handedness, age and date-of-study can re-identify people in small cohorts. A real project needs a formal risk assessment (expert determination or safe-harbor review).
  • Date shifting is not anonymization: whoever holds the salt can reverse it. Store the salt separately from the data (secrets manager), restrict access, and rotate per study.
  • Signal content (e.g. ECG-like artifacts, speech in audio channels, free text in annotations) is not scrubbed.
  • The API has no authentication or audit log. Put it behind an authenticating proxy, add role-based access, TLS and access logging before serving anything but public data.
  • Storage: encrypt at rest (S3 SSE-KMS / disk encryption) and keep the identified originals, if they must exist, in a separate access-controlled location.
  • Consent and data-use agreements determine what may be shared; software cannot decide that.

docs.title: eegkit.pipeline
docs.text:
Batch pipeline: preprocess -> epoch -> analyze for many subjects, with caching.

Layout under paths.output_dir::

cache/sub-001/{epochs-epo.fif, stage1.json, bandpower.csv, psd.npz, erders.npz, ...}
subjects/sub-001/{status.json, qc.json, bandpower.csv, erders_summary.csv,
                  decoding.json, figures/*.png, report.md}
group/{decoding.csv, erders_summary.csv, summary.json, figures/*.png}

Each stage stores a hash of everything it depends on (config sections + input files); a stage is skipped when the stored hash matches and its outputs exist.

docs.title: eegkit.deidentify
docs.text:
De-identification of recording metadata (a demonstration, not a HIPAA certification).

Approach (see docs/privacy.md):

  • direct identifiers (names, birthday, record numbers, experimenter, device serial/site, free-text description) are removed or replaced by a keyed pseudonym;
  • measurement dates are shifted by a per-subject offset derived from an HMAC of the subject label with a secret salt, so intervals within a subject (and between its runs) are preserved but absolute dates cannot be recovered without the salt;
  • the birthday is dropped; :func:age_years gives an integer age at recording (capped at 89);
  • :func:scan_for_identifiers lets callers (and tests) prove that given terms no longer occur.

docs.title: get_salt()
docs.text: Secret salt from $EEGKIT_DEID_SALT (a demo salt, with a warning, if unset).

docs.title: date_offset_days(subject_label, salt)
docs.text: Deterministic per-subject backwards shift in [MIN_SHIFT_DAYS, MAX_SHIFT_DAYS].

docs.title: pseudonym(subject_label, salt)
docs.text: Stable keyed pseudonym (P-xxxxxxxx) that cannot be reversed without the salt.

docs.title: age_years(raw)
docs.text:
Age at recording in whole years (capped at 89), or None if unknown.

Call this before :func:deidentify_raw (which drops the birthday) if the age is needed, e.g. for participants.tsv.

docs.title: deidentify_raw(raw, subject_label, salt=None)
docs.text: Return a de-identified copy of raw (the input is not modified).

docs.title: scan_for_identifiers(raw, terms)
docs.text:
Locations where any of terms (case-insensitive) still appear in the metadata.

Searches every field of raw.info (including nested dicts), the annotation reference time and annotation descriptions. An empty list means none of the terms were found.

docs.title: deidentify_metadata(meta, subject_label, salt=None)
docs.text:
De-identify a flat/nested metadata dict (e.g. a participants row or catalog record).

Identifying keys are dropped, date-like values are shifted by the subject's offset, and the subject id is replaced by its pseudonym.

docs.title: Chunk dataclass
docs.text:
A block of consecutive samples as delivered by the device.

seq increases by one per chunk produced, so a gap between consecutive received chunks means chunks were lost. start_sample is the index of the first sample in the continuous stream; markers holds (stream_sample_index, label) events inside it.

docs.title: eegkit.realtime.buffer
docs.text: Thread-safe multichannel ring buffer with overflow accounting.

docs.title: RingBuffer
docs.text:
Fixed-capacity (n_channels, capacity) circular buffer.

Two ways to read:

  • :meth:latest - the most recent n samples, non-consuming (for display/windowing);
  • :meth:read_new - samples not yet consumed, advancing a read cursor. If the writer laps the reader, the oldest unread samples are overwritten and counted in :attr:overflow_samples (the data is lost, never silently).

docs.title: __len__()
docs.text: Number of valid samples currently held.

docs.title: append(data)
docs.text: Append (n_channels, n) samples; older data is overwritten when full.

docs.title: latest(n)
docs.text: The most recent n samples (fewer if not yet available), oldest first.

docs.title: read_new()
docs.text: All unread samples (oldest first); advances the read cursor.

docs.title: eegkit.realtime.mock
docs.text: MockAmplifier: replays pre-recorded EEG in chunks at the real sampling rate.

docs.title: MockAmplifier
docs.text:
Bases: AcquisitionDevice

Simulated amplifier streaming data ((n_ch, n_samples), volts) in real time.

  • Timing: chunk k is released at t0 + k * chunk_dt (absolute deadlines), so scheduling jitter does not accumulate into drift. speed > 1 compresses time (handy in tests); 1.0 is real time.
  • Ring buffer: every delivered sample is also written to :attr:buffer (the device's recent history, e.g. for display) - independent of how fast consumers read chunks.
  • Markers: stimulus markers ((sample, label) pairs, repeated each loop) plus user markers from :meth:send_marker; each chunk carries the markers inside it.
  • Faults (for testing consumers): :meth:inject_drop, :meth:inject_disconnect, and a bounded chunk queue that discards the oldest chunk when the consumer is too slow - like a real device FIFO, the producer never blocks.

docs.title: chunk_dt property
docs.text: Wall-clock seconds between chunks.

docs.title: from_raw(raw, **kwargs) classmethod
docs.text: Stream the EEG channels of raw; left/right (or T1/T2) annotations become markers.

docs.title: inject_drop(chunk_indices)
docs.text: Lose the chunks with these sequence numbers (never delivered or buffered).

docs.title: inject_disconnect(after_chunks)
docs.text: Disconnect once after_chunks chunks have been produced in total.

docs.title: eegkit.realtime.online
docs.text: Online sliding-window mu/beta band power from a device's chunk stream.

docs.title: PowerResult dataclass
docs.text: Band power for one analysis window. powers[channel][band] is in V².

docs.title: OnlineProcessor
docs.text:
Sliding-window band power at selected channels.

Chunks go through optional common-average re-referencing (needs the full channel set), channel selection and a ring buffer; every hop_s of new data a Hann-windowed periodogram of the last window_s is integrated over each band.

Failure handling:

  • dropped/overflowed chunks - detected by a gap in Chunk.seq. The window is reset instead of bridged, so no spectrum is ever computed across a discontinuity; output resumes once a full window of contiguous data has refilled.
  • device disconnect / end of stream - :meth:run stops cleanly and records the cause in :attr:stats (status).

docs.title: process_chunk(chunk)
docs.text: Feed one chunk; return the results (usually 0 or 1) it completed.

docs.title: run(device, on_result=None, read_timeout=0.1)
docs.text: Blocking loop: read chunks until stopped, disconnected or the stream ends.

docs.title: start(device, on_result=None)
docs.text: Run in a background thread.

docs.title: Tutorial: from raw EEG to ERD/ERS and decoding¶
docs.text: This notebook walks through the eegkit building blocks on subject 1 of the PhysioNet EEGBCI motor-imagery dataset (imagining closing the left vs. right fist, 3 runs, 64 channels, 160 Hz). Every step is also what eegkit run does for all subjects.

docs.title: 1. Look at the raw signal¶
docs.text: Cue markers (dashed) are the left/right imagery onsets.

docs.title: 2. Preprocess¶
docs.text: Band-pass 1-40 Hz, 60 Hz notch, robust bad-channel detection (flat / high variance), average reference. Every function returns a copy.

docs.title: 3. Epoch and reject artifacts¶
docs.text: Epochs span -1.5...4.5 s around each cue; rejection looks at the sensorimotor channels.

docs.title: 4. Spectra and band power¶
docs.text: Mu (8-13 Hz) at C3 drops during right-hand imagery - the contralateral hemisphere.

docs.title: 5. ERD/ERS¶
docs.text: Percent power change relative to the -1...0 s baseline: negative = event-related desynchronization (ERD). The brief red patch right after the cue is the evoked response, not an ERS.

docs.title: 7. Decoding left vs right¶
docs.text: CSP spatial filters + LDA, 5-fold stratified cross-validation; filters are fitted inside each training fold only.

docs.title: 8. The same signal, online¶
docs.text: Replay the recording through the simulated amplifier (8x faster than real time here) and compute sliding-window band power at C3/C4 as a real-time system would.

docs.title: eegkit index
docs.text:
Builds/refreshes outputs/catalog.sqlite from the BIDS dataset and the pipeline outputs:

  • runs (sampling rate, channel count, duration, cue counts, de-identified acquisition time, storage key), channels, subjects, sessions;
  • processing status from each subject's status.json (unprocessed / ok / failed);
  • artifacts - epochs, band power, ERD maps, PSDs - copied into storage under bids/derivatives/eegkit/sub-XXX/.

It is idempotent: run it again after eegkit run.

docs.title: eegkit serve
docs.text:
eegkit serve [-c config.yaml] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8000]

Interactive OpenAPI docs: http://localhost:8000/docs.

Endpoint Purpose GET /recordings filter by subject, task, status, min/max_sampling_rate, min_duration_s, min_channels; paginated GET /recordings/{id} one recording with channels GET /subjects, /subjects/{label} subjects and registered result files GET /subjects/{label}/status processing status, epochs kept, accuracy, bad channels, error GET /subjects/{label}/bandpower band power rows, filter by band, condition, channel GET /subjects/{label}/epochs streamed download of the cleaned epochs (.fif) 
curl "localhost:8000/recordings?status=ok&min_channels=64&limit=5"
curl "localhost:8000/subjects/sub-001/bandpower?band=mu&channel=C3"
curl -OJ localhost:8000/subjects/sub-001/epochs

Status codes: 404 unknown subject/recording or missing result, 409 subject not processed yet, 422 invalid parameter.

Warning

The demo API has no authentication. See Privacy.

docs.title: Storage backends
docs.text: The catalog stores keys, resolved by a Storage: LocalStorage (default, rejects keys that escape the root, including via symlinks) or S3Storage(bucket, prefix, endpoint_url=...) for AWS S3 / MinIO. Implement eegkit.storage.Storage to add another backend.

docs.title: eegkit run
docs.text:
eegkit run -c configs/default.yaml [-s 1,2] [--force]

For every subject: load (BIDS if present, else raw EDF) -> preprocess -> epoch -> reject -> band power, PSD, ERD/ERS, CSP+LDA decoding -> per-subject tables and figures. Then the group level: mean ERD/ERS maps, mean PSD, geometric-mean band-power topomaps, decoding table.

sub-001  ok     epochs=45  dropped=0   acc=0.78 (cached: epochs,analysis)
...
Group: n=10  decoding 0.624 ± 0.169  -> outputs/group

Caching. There are two stages, each storing a hash of everything it depends on:

  1. epochs - preprocess config, epoch config, runs, input file names and sizes;
  2. analysis - the epochs hash plus the analysis config.

Rerunning skips a stage whose hash is unchanged: change only analysis.bands and just the analysis is recomputed; change a filter and everything is. --force ignores the cache.

Failures are isolated per subject: a subject that fails is recorded in status.json with the error, the rest continue, and the exit code is 1.

docs.title: eegkit report
docs.text:
eegkit report --subject 2

Writes outputs/subjects/sub-002/report.md - quality control (bad channels, dropped epochs), decoding accuracy, mu-band ERD table, and the three figures.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All commands accept -c/--config path.yaml. Every key is optional; defaults live in configs/default.yaml. The file is validated with pydantic: unknown keys, reversed ranges, bad subject ids or run numbers abort with a readable message and exit code 2.

Section Key Default Meaning top subjects 1-10 subject ids (1-109) top runs [4, 8, 12] left/right-fist imagery runs paths raw_dir, bids_root, output_dir, cache_dir, catalog_db, storage_root data/..., outputs/... locations privacy deidentify true strip identifiers / shift dates when converting to BIDS preprocess l_freq, h_freq, notch_freqs 1, 40, [60] filters (Hz) preprocess flat_std_v, noisy_z, interpolate_bads 1e-7, 4.0, true bad-channel detection epochs tmin, tmax, baseline -1.5, 4.5, (-1.5, 0) epoch window (s) epochs reject_uv, reject_channels 300, sensorimotor ROI peak-to-peak rejection analysis bands, band_window mu 8-13, beta 13-30; 0.5-3.5 s band power analysis erders_* C3/C4, 6-30 Hz, baseline -1...0 s ERD/ERS maps analysis.decoding tmin, tmax, fmin, fmax, n_components, n_splits, seed 0.5-2.5 s, 8-30 Hz, 4, 5, 42 CSP+LDA

Why the rejection uses a channel subset

EEGBCI is high-amplitude data: blinks give > 300 µV at frontal sites in almost every epoch. Rejection and decoding are therefore evaluated on 15 medial sensorimotor channels (SENSORIMOTOR in eegkit.config); the motor rhythms analysed are not affected by frontal blinks, and discarding every epoch with a blink would leave too few trials.

docs.title: eegkit download
docs.text:
eegkit download [-c config.yaml] [-s 1,2,3]

Downloads the configured runs (default 4, 8, 12 = left vs. right fist imagery) of the configured subjects from PhysioNet through mne.datasets.eegbci. Existing files are reused. -s overrides the subject list for this call only.

docs.title: eegkit to-bids
docs.text:
eegkit to-bids [-c config.yaml] [-s ...] [--overwrite]

Converts the EDFs to a BIDS EEG dataset with mne-bids:

data/bids/
  dataset_description.json  participants.tsv  README
  sub-001/ses-01/
    sub-001_ses-01_scans.tsv
    eeg/sub-001_ses-01_task-motorimagery_run-04_eeg.edf
        ..._events.tsv  ..._channels.tsv  ..._electrodes.tsv  ..._eeg.json
  • Channel names are standardized (Fc5. -> FC5) and the standard 10-05 montage is applied.
  • Events are named rest, left, right.
  • With privacy.deidentify: true (default) recordings are de-identified first - dates are shifted and identifiers removed. Set EEGKIT_DEID_SALT (see Privacy).
  • Existing runs are skipped unless --overwrite.

docs.title: GUI: app
docs.text:
eegkit app [-c config.yaml] [--port 8501] [--headless]

Needs a catalog (eegkit index) for the Explorer; the Live monitor also works with a built-in synthetic signal.

docs.title: Explorer
docs.text:
Pick a subject and run from the catalog (sidebar). Tabs:

  • Raw traces - scrollable window, channel selection, scale, cue markers;
  • PSD - left vs. right spectra at chosen channels, mu/beta shaded;
  • ERD/ERS - time-frequency maps at C3/C4, adjustable colour scale;
  • Topomaps - mu/beta power per condition and the right-minus-left contrast.

docs.title: Live monitor
docs.text: Start/stop a MockAmplifier replaying a subject (or synthetic data) at 0.5x/1x/2x. Shows the scrolling C3/Cz/C4 signal with cue markers, band-power bars from the online processor, and device/processor state, latency and dropped/overflowed chunk counters. Simulate disconnect demonstrates the failure handling; Insert marker adds a user event.

docs.title: Real-time simulation
docs.text:
Not a CLI command - a library layer (eegkit.realtime) used by the GUI and the tutorial.

from eegkit.realtime import MockAmplifier, OnlineProcessor

amp = MockAmplifier.from_raw(raw, chunk_samples=16)  # 100 ms chunks at 160 Hz
proc = OnlineProcessor(amp.ch_names, amp.sfreq, window_s=1.0, hop_s=0.25)
amp.start()
proc.start(amp, on_result=lambda r: print(r.time_s, r.powers["C3"]["mu"]))
Piece Role AcquisitionDevice (ABC) start/stop/read_chunk/send_marker/stats - what a real driver implements MockAmplifier replays data at the real rate using absolute deadlines (no drift); history ring buffer; stimulus + user markers; fault injection RingBuffer thread-safe; read cursor with explicit overflow accounting OnlineProcessor common-average reference, sliding Hann periodogram, mu/beta power at C3/C4

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
Failure Behaviour Dropped chunk Chunk.seq gap is detected; the window is reset (never a spectrum across a discontinuity); counted in stats.dropped_chunks Device disconnect buffered chunks are delivered, then DeviceDisconnectedError; the processor stops with status="disconnected"; start() reconnects Consumer too slow the device FIFO drops its oldest chunk (producer never blocks) and counts it; ring buffer counts overwritten unread samples

Measured on real 64-channel data: ~2 ms mean latency from chunk emission to band-power result.
